headline: High-risk filesystem and Git overlap in ECC; Taipy’s no-egress profile reduces leakage but not conflict or cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write the filesystem, use MCP, and run browsers, so it can ingest content that may be treated as instructions. Taipy exposes no I/O surfaces, so the pair lacks a documented direct bridge, but ECC’s shared files and MCP make prompt injection plausible if Taipy outputs are copied into ECC-managed files.
conditions: IF Taipy outputs are copied into files or prompts that ECC reads via filesystem or stdin/stdout, injection becomes reachable.
IF ECC MCP configs or hooks consume Taipy-generated text as instructions, the pathway is active.
mitigations: Keep Taipy outputs in a separate read-only folder.
Disable ECC hooks for untrusted text ingestion.
Require a human review step before copying Taipy output into ECC prompts.
Use explicit delimiters and instruction-stripping for imported text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for Taipy-originated content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, git history, and security findings, so it can handle sensitive local data. Taipy has network_egress:none and no documented I/O surfaces, so there is no clear exfiltration path from the pair by default. The main risk is local workspace exposure if both share files, which appears possible only through external setup.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace, ECC may read Taipy artifacts locally.
IF an operator copies sensitive Taipy inputs into ECC-managed files, those data can be retained in ECC session state.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Store sensitive inputs outside ECC-managed directories.
Turn off ECC session retention for sensitive runs.
Review and redact shared files before opening them in ECC.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has unrestricted filesystem write, git-state modification, and subprocess/network capabilities; Taipy is a data-engineering automation framework that may also mutate shared project state when orchestrated externally. Because both can plausibly act on the same repository or workspace, write conflicts and git corruption are credible in default multi-agent setups, and the rubric says uncertainty escalates.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, concurrent writes can race.
IF Taipy is configured to modify shared project files while ECC edits the same tree, conflicts can corrupt state.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Pause one agent before the other edits git state.
Use branches instead of direct shared commits.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate and modify code, docs, and security findings, while Taipy is a data-engineering/automation system that may consume upstream outputs. If Taipy treats ECC output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream workflows. Taipy’s lack of documented verification controls keeps this above low, though the exact interaction is not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Taipy ingests ECC-produced files or reports without validation, downstream actions can propagate mistakes.
IF ECC-generated security findings are used as inputs to Taipy automation, false positives or hallucinations can cascade.
mitigations: Require validation before Taipy consumes ECC outputs.
Add checksum or schema checks on exchanged files.
Keep ECC outputs advisory, not authoritative.
Review high-impact outputs manually before automation.
requires-engineering: implement provenance and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly handles session retention, hooks, and security findings, which can create retention or logging concerns. Taipy’s profile shows no data classes touched and no residency or compliance commitments, so there is no documented mismatch beyond generic policy risk. The other agent is not cited because no specific compliance surface is exposed in its profile.
conditions: IF ECC retention settings store regulated data longer than policy allows, compliance risk appears.
IF Taipy is used with regulated inputs and no retention controls are added, policy mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Set ECC retention to the minimum needed.
Avoid placing regulated data in ECC session artifacts.
Document a retention policy for exchanged files.
Review hook logs for sensitive content.
requires-engineering: add compliance-specific data handling controls.
